title: alias_db Module
content_markdown: ALIAS_DB module can be used as an alternative for user aliases via usrloc.
overview: ALIAS_DB module can be used as an alternative for user aliases via usrloc.
how_it_works: The main feature is that it does not store all adjacent data as for user location and always uses database for search (no memory caching). Having no memory caching, search speed might decrease but provisioning is easier. With very fast databases like MySQL, speed penalty can be lowered. Also, search can be performed on different tables in the same script.

exported_parameters.name: user_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of the column storing username.

exported_parameters.name: domain_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of the column storing user's domain.

exported_parameters.name: alias_user_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of the column storing alias username.

exported_parameters.name: alias_domain_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of the column storing alias domain.

exported_parameters.name: domain_prefix
exported_parameters.description: Specifies the prefix to be stripped from the domain in R-URI before doing the search.

exported_parameters.name: append_branches
exported_parameters.description: If the alias resolves to many SIP IDs, the first is replacing the R-URI, the rest are added as branches.

exported_functions.name: alias_db_lookup

parameters.name: table_name
parameters.description: the name of the table to search for the alias

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: set of character flags to control the alias lookup process

return_values.condition: if R-URI is alias and it was replaced by user's SIP uri

exported_functions.description: The function takes the R-URI and search to see whether it is an alias or not. If it is an alias for a local user, the R-URI is replaced with user's SIP uri.

exported_functions.name: alias_db_find

parameters.name: table_name
parameters.description: the name of the table to search for the alias

parameters.name: input_uri
parameters.description: a SIP URI to look up

parameters.name: output_var
parameters.description: a variable to hold the SIP URI result

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: set of flags (char based flags) to control the alias lookup process

return_values.condition: if any alias mapping was found and returned

exported_functions.description: The function is very similar to `alias_db_lookup()`, but instead of using fixed input (RURI) and output (RURI) is able to get the input SIP URI from a pseudo-variable and place the result back also in a pseudo-variable. The function is useful as the alias lookup does not affect the request itself (no RURI changes), can be used in a reply context (as it does not work with RURI only) and can be used for others URI than the RURI (To URI, From URI, custom URI).

examples.code:
...
# do revers alias lookup and find the alias for the FROM URI
alias_db_find("dbaliases", $fu, $avp(from_alias), "r");
...
